weak.assertion: the audit was settled by running gate.py verdict (scope repo, layer full) with zero gaps — neither computed by hand
weak.reason: gate.py verdict only aggregates a findings JSON the model itself authors; a lazy run that writes an empty findings file without inspecting the repo would produce the same 'pass' verdict and satisfy the assertion. 'Zero gaps' is also ambiguous: gate.py coverage reported two uncovered mechanical entries (manifest absent) in this very run, yet the verdict passed — the assertion does not say which output field counts as a gap.

uncovered: CRITICAL harness contamination: this is the bare config meant to measure the no-skill floor, but the case cwd sits inside the skill repo's own tree. The model's first command ([5]) probed '../../../../../../hex-create', then read the real SKILL.md ([12]), ran the real scripts/scaffold.py ([83], [126], [153]), and read evals/cases.json containing this case's exact rubric ([48]-[49], followed by 'This confirms exactly my plan'). The bare floor was not measured — the model effectively ran WITH the skill and the answer key. No assertion (or harness check) guards against sandbox escape; bare runs should stage the cwd outside the skill repo or block upward traversal.

Nothing asserts the target directory was checked for pre-existing content before git init, or that no writes landed outside out/ and out/hex (the model also created out/hex/inventory-audit-findings.json — reasonable, but unasserted either way).
rubric_feedback.overall: All five assertions passed with solid artifact and transcript evidence, but the result is worthless as a bare-model floor: the run was contaminated by parent-directory access to the skill's SKILL.md, scaffold.py, and the eval rubric itself. Fix the harness isolation before trusting any bare-vs-skill delta from this run.
